{{Short description|Depth of nesting of quantifiers in a formula}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2025}}
In [[mathematical logic]], the '''quantifier rank''' of a [[Formula (mathematical logic)|formula]] is the depth of nesting of its [[Quantifier (logic)|quantifiers]]. It plays an essential role in [[model theory]].

The quantifier rank is a property of the formula itself (i.e. the expression in a language).  Thus two [[Logical equivalence|logically equivalent]] formulae can have different quantifier ranks, when they express the same thing in different ways.

==Definition==

=== In first-order logic ===
Let <math>\varphi</math> be a [[First-order logic|first-order]] formula. The quantifier rank of <math>\varphi</math>, written <math>\operatorname{qr}(\varphi)</math>, is defined as:

* <math>\operatorname{qr}(\varphi) = 0</math>, if <math>\varphi</math> is atomic.
* <math>\operatorname{qr}(\varphi_1 \land \varphi_2) = \operatorname{qr}(\varphi_1 \lor \varphi_2) = \max(\operatorname{qr}(\varphi_1), \operatorname{qr}(\varphi_2))</math>.
* <math>\operatorname{qr}(\lnot \varphi) = \operatorname{qr}(\varphi)</math>.
* <math>\operatorname{qr}(\exists_x \varphi) = \operatorname{qr}(\varphi) + 1</math>.
* <math>\operatorname{qr}(\forall_x \varphi) = \operatorname{qr}(\varphi) + 1</math>.

'''Remarks'''
* We write <math>\operatorname{FO}[n]</math> for the set of all [[first-order formula]]s <math>\varphi</math> with <math>\operatorname{qr}(\varphi) \le n</math>.
* Relational <math>\operatorname{FO}[n]</math> (without function symbols) is always of finite size, i.e. contains a finite number of formulas.
* In [[prenex normal form]], the quantifier rank of <math>\varphi</math> is exactly the number of quantifiers appearing in <math>\varphi</math>.

=== In higher-order logic ===
For [[fixed-point logic]], with a least fixed-point operator <math>\operatorname{LFP}</math>: <math>\operatorname{qr}([\operatorname{LFP}_\phi]y) = 1 + \operatorname{qr}( \phi )</math>.

==Examples==
* A sentence of quantifier rank 2:
: <math>\forall x\exists y R(x, y)</math> 
* A formula of quantifier rank 1:
: <math>\forall x R(y, x) \wedge \exists x R(x, y)</math>
* A formula of quantifier rank 0:
: <math>R(x, y) \wedge x \neq y</math>
* A sentence in [[prenex normal form]] of quantifier rank 3:
: <math>\forall x \exists y \exists z ((x \neq y \wedge x R y) \wedge (x \neq z \wedge z R x)) </math> 
* A sentence, equivalent to the previous, although of quantifier rank 2:
: <math>\forall x (\exists y (x \neq y \wedge x R y)) \wedge \exists z (x \neq z \wedge z R x )) </math>
